metadata.title: Hypertension in pregnancy: diagnosis and management
metadata.summary: This guideline addresses the diagnosis, assessment and management of hypertension during pregnancy, labour, birth and the postnatal period, including gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia. It also covers care for women with hypertension who are planning pregnancy and follow-up after a pregnancy affected by hypertension. Its recommendations address maternal treatment, fetal monitoring, timing of birth and care during breastfeeding.

target_population: Women with hypertension who wish to conceive
Pregnant women with hypertension or at risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
Women who have had a pregnancy complicated by hypertension
Babies of women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
therapeutic_areas: Follow-up and counselling about future pregnancy and cardiovascular risk

management.actions: Stop treatment, preferably within 2 working days of being notified of the pregnancy, and offer an alternative.

prevention: Advise women planning pregnancy to discuss alternative antihypertensive treatment with the professional managing their hypertension. Women taking these medicines for another condition, such as renal disease, should discuss alternatives with the professional managing that condition.
toxicities.dose_modifications: Stop treatment if pregnancy occurs, preferably within 2 working days of notification.

toxicities.event: Possible congenital abnormalities and neonatal complications
prevention: Advise women planning pregnancy that these risks may be increased and to discuss alternative antihypertensive treatment with the professional managing their hypertension.

toxicities.event: Neonatal skeletal adverse effects, hypocalcaemia and hypermagnesemia
recognition: Abnormal neonatal calcium or magnesium levels

management.severity: Prolonged or repeated use during pregnancy
management.actions: Consider monitoring the neonate for abnormal calcium and magnesium levels and skeletal adverse effects. Maternal administration for longer than 5 to 7 days in pregnancy has been associated with these neonatal effects.

toxicities.event: Possible low blood pressure in a breastfed baby

management.severity: Baby with symptoms of low blood pressure during the first few weeks
management.actions: Consider monitoring the baby's blood pressure, particularly if the baby was born preterm. Advise the woman to watch for the listed symptoms after discharge. If an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist is used during breastfeeding, carefully follow the infant for possible hypotension.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise daily aspirin 75 mg to 150 mg to reduce the risk of pre-eclampsia. High risk is indicated by hypertensive disease in a previous pregnancy, chronic kidney disease, autoimmune disease such as systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome, type 1 or type 2 diabetes, or chronic hypertension. Aspirin for prevention of pre-eclampsia in pregnancy must be prescribed in England rather than sold as a pharmacy medicine.
prophylaxis.target_population: Pregnant women at high risk of pre-eclampsia
prophylaxis.duration: From 12 weeks until the birth of the baby

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise daily aspirin 75 mg to 150 mg to reduce the risk of pre-eclampsia when more than 1 moderate risk factor is present: nulliparity, age 40 years or older, an interval between pregnancies of more than 10 years, BMI of 35 kg/m2 or more at the first visit, a family history of pre-eclampsia, or multi-fetal pregnancy. Aspirin for prevention of pre-eclampsia in pregnancy must be prescribed in England rather than sold as a pharmacy medicine.
prophylaxis.target_population: Pregnant women with more than 1 moderate risk factor for pre-eclampsia
prophylaxis.duration: From 12 weeks until the birth of the baby

prophylaxis.recommendation: Offer aspirin 75 mg to 150 mg once daily.
Do not use nitric oxide donors, progesterone, diuretics or low molecular weight heparin to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.
Do not recommend magnesium, folic acid, antioxidants (vitamins C and E), fish oils or algal oils, or garlic solely to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.
Do not recommend restricting salt during pregnancy solely to prevent gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia.
Give the same advice about rest, exercise and work as is given to healthy pregnant women.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women with chronic hypertension or at risk of hypertensive disorders during pregnancy

prophylaxis.recommendation: Consider intravenous magnesium sulfate if birth is planned within 24 hours. Also consider whether magnesium sulfate is needed when 1 or more of the following are present: ongoing or recurrent severe headaches, visual scotomata, nausea or vomiting, epigastric pain, oliguria with severe hypertension, or progressively worsening blood-test results. If administered, use the Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen: 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes, followed by 1 g/hour.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women with severe pre-eclampsia in a critical care setting
prophylaxis.duration: Maintain the infusion for 24 hours; following an eclamptic fit, continue it for 24 hours after the last fit

prophylaxis.recommendation: Offer a course of antenatal corticosteroids in line with the NICE guideline on preterm labour and birth if early birth is considered likely within 7 days. If early birth is planned for preterm pre-eclampsia, offer antenatal corticosteroids if indicated; when planned early birth is necessary for chronic or gestational hypertension, offer a course if indicated. For pre-eclampsia before 34 weeks, the timing-of-birth guidance also calls for a course alongside continued surveillance unless early birth is indicated; from 34 weeks to 36 weeks plus 6 days, consider a course when weighing planned early birth.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women with pre-eclampsia when early birth is considered likely within 7 days, and women for whom planned early birth requires antenatal corticosteroids as indicated

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise discussion with a GP or specialist about reducing later cardiovascular risk, including avoiding smoking, maintaining a healthy lifestyle and maintaining a healthy weight.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women who have had a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy

prophylaxis.type: Body mass index and recurrence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise achieving and maintaining a BMI in the healthy range of 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2 before the next pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: aspirin
approved_indications: Prevention of pre-eclampsia in pregnant women with any high-risk factor or more than 1 moderate-risk factor.
Prevention of pre-eclampsia in pregnant women with chronic hypertension.
therapies_index.administration: 75 mg to 150 mg daily from 12 weeks until the birth of the baby for women at increased risk of pre-eclampsia; 75 mg to 150 mg once daily from 12 weeks for women with chronic hypertension. For these indications, aspirin must be prescribed rather than sold as a pharmacy medicine in England.

therapies_index.name: labetalol
approved_indications: Consider for chronic hypertension in pregnancy.
Consider for gestational hypertension.
Offer for hypertension in pregnant women with pre-eclampsia.
Treat severe hypertension in critical care during pregnancy or after birth.
Consider as an addition to, or replacement for 1 medicine in, postnatal combination treatment when blood pressure remains uncontrolled.
therapies_index.administration: Oral or intravenous for severe hypertension in critical care; no dose is specified. The guideline notes administration 2 to 4 times daily when comparing postnatal treatment options.
monitoring: During critical care treatment for severe hypertension, assess the blood-pressure response and adverse effects in the woman and baby, and adjust treatment accordingly.

therapies_index.name: nifedipine
approved_indications: Consider for chronic hypertension in pregnancy when labetalol is unsuitable.
Consider for gestational hypertension when labetalol is unsuitable.
Offer for hypertension with pre-eclampsia when labetalol is unsuitable.
Treat severe hypertension in critical care during pregnancy or after birth.
Consider for postnatal hypertension in women of black African or Caribbean family origin.
Consider with enalapril when postnatal blood pressure is not controlled by a single medicine.
therapies_index.administration: Oral for severe hypertension in critical care; no dose is specified.
monitoring: During critical care treatment for severe hypertension, assess the blood-pressure response and adverse effects in the woman and baby, and adjust treatment accordingly.

therapies_index.name: methyldopa
approved_indications: Consider for chronic hypertension in pregnancy if labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.
Consider for gestational hypertension if labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.
Offer for hypertension with pre-eclampsia if labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.
therapies_index.administration: If used during pregnancy, stop within 2 days after the birth and change to another antihypertensive treatment if needed.
key_toxicities: The committee notes that methyldopa may cause more side effects than the other preferred pregnancy options.

therapies_index.name: enalapril
approved_indications: Offer for postnatal hypertension.
Consider with nifedipine or amlodipine when postnatal blood pressure is not controlled by a single medicine.
The cited MHRA clarification says its use may be considered, with careful infant follow-up, when an ACE inhibitor is necessary for a mother breastfeeding an older infant.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline favours its once-daily administration for postnatal treatment; no dose is specified.
monitoring: Monitor maternal renal function and maternal serum potassium during postnatal treatment.
For an exposed breastfed infant, the cited MHRA clarification recommends careful follow-up for possible hypotension.

therapies_index.name: amlodipine
approved_indications: Consider for postnatal hypertension in women of black African or Caribbean family origin if previous use successfully controlled their blood pressure.
Consider with enalapril when postnatal blood pressure is not controlled by a single medicine.

therapies_index.name: atenolol
approved_indications: For postnatal hypertension inadequately controlled by nifedipine or amlodipine with enalapril, consider adding atenolol or replacing 1 of the existing medicines with it if the combination is ineffective or not tolerated.

therapies_index.name: hydralazine
approved_indications: Treat severe hypertension in critical care during pregnancy or after birth.
therapies_index.administration: Intravenous; during the antenatal period, consider up to 500 ml crystalloid fluid before or alongside the first intravenous dose.
monitoring: During critical care treatment, assess the blood-pressure response and adverse effects in the woman and baby, and adjust treatment accordingly.

therapies_index.name: magnesium sulfate
approved_indications: Give intravenously in critical care to a woman with severe hypertension or severe pre-eclampsia who has had an eclamptic fit.
Consider intravenously for severe pre-eclampsia in critical care when birth is planned within 24 hours.
Consider treatment when features of severe pre-eclampsia specified in the guideline are present.
Offer intravenously when early birth is planned for preterm pre-eclampsia, if indicated; use before planned early birth for chronic or gestational hypertension if indicated.
therapies_index.administration: Use the Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen: 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes, then 1 g/hour for 24 hours; after an eclamptic fit, continue the infusion for 24 hours after the last fit. Treat recurrent fits with a further 2 g to 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes.
key_toxicities: Maternal administration for longer than 5 to 7 days in pregnancy has been associated with neonatal skeletal adverse effects, hypocalcaemia and hypermagnesemia.
monitoring: If maternal use during pregnancy is prolonged or repeated, consider monitoring the neonate for abnormal calcium and magnesium levels and skeletal adverse effects.

therapies_index.name: Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen
approved_indications: Administration regimen for magnesium sulfate in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia when treatment is indicated.
therapies_index.administration: Give 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes, followed by 1 g/hour for 24 hours. After an eclamptic fit, continue the infusion for 24 hours after the last fit. For recurrent fits, give another 2 g to 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes.
key_toxicities: Prolonged or repeated magnesium sulfate exposure during pregnancy has been associated with neonatal skeletal adverse effects, hypocalcaemia and hypermagnesemia.
monitoring: For prolonged or repeated exposure during pregnancy, consider neonatal monitoring of calcium and magnesium levels and skeletal adverse effects.

therapies_index.name: nifedipine (or amlodipine) and enalapril
approved_indications: Consider nifedipine with enalapril, or amlodipine with enalapril, when a single medicine does not control postnatal hypertension.
monitoring: Monitor maternal renal function and maternal serum potassium when using enalapril.

therapies_index.name: antenatal corticosteroids
approved_indications: Offer a course when indicated before planned early birth in women with chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension or preterm pre-eclampsia.
Offer a course if early birth is considered likely within 7 days in a woman with pre-eclampsia.
Consider a course when weighing planned early birth from 34 weeks to 36 weeks plus 6 days in a woman with pre-eclampsia.
therapies_index.administration: A course is specified, but the guideline does not give a drug, dose or route.

therapies_index.name: angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors
therapies_index.administration: If a woman becomes pregnant while taking an ACE inhibitor, stop it preferably within 2 working days of notification of pregnancy and offer an alternative.
key_toxicities: Use during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of congenital abnormalities.
monitoring: The cited MHRA clarification recommends careful follow-up of a breastfed infant for possible hypotension when an ACE inhibitor is considered necessary for the mother.

therapies_index.name: angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs)
therapies_index.administration: If a woman becomes pregnant while taking an ARB, stop it preferably within 2 working days of notification of pregnancy and offer an alternative. Where possible, avoid use for postnatal hypertension during breastfeeding or milk expression.
key_toxicities: Use during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of congenital abnormalities.

therapies_index.name: thiazide or thiazide-like diuretics
key_toxicities: Use during pregnancy may increase the risk of congenital abnormalities and neonatal complications.

therapies_index.name: diuretics
therapies_index.administration: Do not use to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy; where possible, avoid for postnatal hypertension during breastfeeding or milk expression.

therapies_index.name: captopril
approved_indications: The cited MHRA clarification says captopril may be considered when an ACE inhibitor is necessary for a mother breastfeeding an older infant.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline describes administration 3 times daily when explaining why enalapril is preferred for postnatal treatment.
monitoring: The cited MHRA clarification recommends careful follow-up of the exposed breastfed infant for possible hypotension.

therapies_index.name: quinapril
approved_indications: The cited MHRA clarification says quinapril may be considered when an ACE inhibitor is necessary for a mother breastfeeding an older infant.
monitoring: The cited MHRA clarification recommends careful follow-up of the exposed breastfed infant for possible hypotension.

therapies_index.name: nitric oxide donors
therapies_index.administration: Do not use to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: progesterone
therapies_index.administration: Do not use to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: low molecular weight heparin
therapies_index.administration: Do not use to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: magnesium
therapies_index.administration: Do not recommend supplementation solely to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: folic acid
therapies_index.administration: Do not recommend supplementation solely to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: antioxidants (vitamins C and E)
therapies_index.administration: Do not recommend supplementation solely to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: fish oils or algal oils
therapies_index.administration: Do not recommend supplementation solely to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: garlic
therapies_index.administration: Do not recommend supplementation solely to prevent hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: diazepam
therapies_index.administration: Do not use instead of magnesium sulfate for women with eclampsia.

therapies_index.name: phenytoin
therapies_index.administration: Do not use instead of magnesium sulfate for women with eclampsia.

therapies_index.name: dexamethasone
therapies_index.administration: Do not use to treat HELLP syndrome.

therapies_index.name: betamethasone
therapies_index.administration: Do not use to treat HELLP syndrome.

therapies_index.name: crystalloid fluid
approved_indications: Consider before or alongside the first intravenous hydralazine dose in the antenatal period.
therapies_index.administration: Up to 500 ml before or at the same time as the first intravenous hydralazine dose.

therapies_index.name: volume expansion
approved_indications: The guideline permits an exception to its restriction on volume expansion in severe pre-eclampsia when hydralazine is the antenatal antihypertensive.
therapies_index.administration: Do not use for severe pre-eclampsia unless hydralazine is the antenatal antihypertensive.

therapies_index.name: maintenance fluids
approved_indications: Fluid maintenance for women with severe pre-eclampsia.
therapies_index.administration: Limit to 80 ml/hour unless there are other continuing fluid losses, such as haemorrhage.

therapies_index.name: low-dose epidural analgesia
approved_indications: Labour analgesia considered for women with severe pre-eclampsia.
therapies_index.administration: Do not preload with intravenous fluids before establishing analgesia in women with severe pre-eclampsia.

therapies_index.name: combined spinal epidural analgesia
approved_indications: Labour analgesia considered for women with severe pre-eclampsia.
therapies_index.administration: Do not preload with intravenous fluids before establishing analgesia in women with severe pre-eclampsia.

therapies_index.name: operative or assisted birth
approved_indications: Consider during the second stage of labour for women whose severe hypertension has not responded to initial treatment.

therapies_index.name: caesarean section
approved_indications: A possible mode of birth for women with severe hypertension, severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia; select the mode according to clinical circumstances and the woman's preference.

therapies_index.name: induction of labour
approved_indications: A possible mode of birth for women with severe hypertension, severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia; select the mode according to clinical circumstances and the woman's preference.

therapies_index.name: planned early birth
approved_indications: Consider before 37 weeks in pre-eclampsia when maternal or fetal indications warrant it.
For chronic or gestational hypertension with blood pressure below 160/110 mmHg, do not offer before 37 weeks unless another medical indication exists.
therapies_index.administration: For pre-eclampsia, continue surveillance before 34 weeks and from 34 weeks to 36 weeks plus 6 days unless an indication for planned early birth arises. From 37 weeks onwards, initiate birth within 24 to 48 hours.

therapies_index.name: weight management
approved_indications: Offer advice to pregnant women with chronic hypertension.

therapies_index.name: exercise
approved_indications: Offer advice to pregnant women with chronic hypertension; provide women with chronic hypertension or at risk of hypertensive disorders the same exercise advice as healthy pregnant women.

therapies_index.name: healthy eating
approved_indications: Offer advice to pregnant women with chronic hypertension.

therapies_index.name: salt restriction
therapies_index.administration: Do not recommend during pregnancy solely to prevent gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia. The guideline separately advises women with chronic hypertension about lowering dietary salt.

therapies_index.name: bed rest in hospital
therapies_index.administration: Do not offer as treatment for gestational hypertension.

conditions.name: Hypertension
conditions.description: Blood pressure of 140 mmHg systolic or higher, or 90 mmHg diastolic or higher, during pregnancy.
conditions.epidemiology: Hypertensive disorders affect around 8% to 10% of all pregnant women.

subtypes.name: Chronic hypertension
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Hypertension present at the booking visit, before 20 weeks, or when the woman is already taking antihypertensive medication on referral to maternity services.

subtypes.name: Gestational hypertension
subtypes.distinguishing_features: New hypertension after 20 weeks without significant proteinuria.

subtypes.name: Pre-eclampsia
subtypes.distinguishing_features: New hypertension after 20 weeks accompanied by specified new-onset proteinuria, maternal organ dysfunction or uteroplacental dysfunction.

subtypes.name: Severe hypertension
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Blood pressure over 160 mmHg systolic or over 110 mmHg diastolic.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify hypertension and assess its severity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During pregnancy and labour, and after birth when monitoring a hypertensive disorder.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Hypertension is 140 mmHg systolic or higher, or 90 mmHg diastolic or higher; severe hypertension is over 160 mmHg systolic or over 110 mmHg diastolic.

long_term_effects: A history of a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy is associated with greater risk of hypertension and cardiovascular disease later in life.
The overall likelihood of a hypertensive disorder recurring in a future pregnancy is approximately 1 in 5.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Women who have had a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy are advised to discuss cardiovascular risk reduction with their GP or specialist.

conditions.name: Chronic hypertension
conditions.description: Hypertension identified at the booking visit or before 20 weeks, or already treated with antihypertensive medication when the woman is referred to maternity services. Its aetiology may be primary or secondary.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess blood pressure control during pregnancy and after birth.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At additional antenatal appointments according to individual needs; after birth, daily for the first 2 days, at least once between day 3 and day 5, and when clinically indicated following a treatment change.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: During treatment in pregnancy, the target is 135/85 mmHg. After birth, the aim is to keep blood pressure lower than 140/90 mmHg.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help rule out pre-eclampsia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When pre-eclampsia is suspected between 20 weeks and 36 weeks and 6 days of pregnancy.

diagnostic_workup.test: Ultrasound for fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume assessment
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At 28 weeks, 32 weeks and 36 weeks.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the fetal circulation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At 28 weeks, 32 weeks and 36 weeks.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Only if clinically indicated.

follow_up.schedule: Additional antenatal appointments depend on maternal and fetal needs; these may be weekly when hypertension is poorly controlled or every 2 to 4 weeks when well controlled. After birth, offer a treatment review at 2 weeks and a medical review at 6 to 8 weeks.
recommended_tests: Measure blood pressure daily for the first 2 days after birth and at least once between day 3 and day 5.
Measure blood pressure as clinically indicated if antihypertensive treatment changes after birth.
long_term_effects: For women with chronic hypertension in a current or previous pregnancy, the table reports an approximately 1.7 times increased risk of a major adverse cardiovascular event and an approximately 1.8 times increased risk of stroke, relative to women without a hypertensive disorder during pregnancy.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Continue antihypertensive treatment after birth if required, with review by a GP or specialist.

conditions.name: Gestational hypertension
conditions.description: Hypertension first appearing after 20 weeks of pregnancy without significant proteinuria.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate gestational hypertension and factors requiring closer assessment and follow-up.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At presentation, by a healthcare professional trained in managing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Factors requiring additional assessment and follow-up include nulliparity, age 40 years or older, pregnancy interval of more than 10 years, family history of pre-eclampsia, multi-fetal pregnancy, BMI of 35 kg/m2 or more, gestational age at presentation, previous pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension, and pre-existing vascular or kidney disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess severity and response to treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: For hypertension, once or twice a week depending on blood pressure until it is 135/85 mmHg or less; for severe hypertension, every 15 to 30 minutes until it is less than 160/110 mmHg.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Once antihypertensive treatment is given, the target is 135/85 mmHg or less.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Monitor for proteinuria.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Once or twice a week alongside blood pressure measurement for hypertension; daily during admission for severe hypertension.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A result of 1+ or more prompts quantification with albumin:creatinine ratio or protein:creatinine ratio.

diagnostic_workup.test: Full blood count, liver function and renal function
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Monitor maternal haematological, liver and kidney status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At presentation and then weekly.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help rule out pre-eclampsia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: On 1 occasion if pre-eclampsia is suspected, between 20 weeks and 36 weeks and 6 days of pregnancy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal heart activity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At every antenatal appointment.

diagnostic_workup.test: Ultrasound for fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume assessment
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis; if findings are normal, repeat every 2 to 4 weeks if clinically indicated. If severe hypertension persists, repeat every 2 weeks.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the fetal circulation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis; if findings are normal, repeat every 2 to 4 weeks if clinically indicated. In severe gestational hypertension, subsequent monitoring is determined by scan findings.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: For gestational hypertension, only if clinically indicated; for severe gestational hypertension, at diagnosis and subsequently if clinically indicated.

follow_up.schedule: After birth, offer women still receiving antihypertensive treatment a medical review 2 weeks after transfer to community care. Offer all women a medical review 6 to 8 weeks after birth.
recommended_tests: Measure blood pressure daily for the first 2 days after birth and at least once between day 3 and day 5.
Measure blood pressure as clinically indicated if antihypertensive treatment changes after birth.
long_term_effects: After gestational hypertension in a previous or current pregnancy, hypertension of any type in a future pregnancy occurs in approximately 22% (1 in 5 women), pre-eclampsia in approximately 7% (1 in 14 women), gestational hypertension in between approximately 11% and 15% (up to 1 in 7 women), and chronic hypertension in approximately 3% (up to 1 in 34 women).

For women with gestational hypertension in a current or previous pregnancy, the table reports an approximately 1.5 to 3 times increased risk of a major adverse cardiovascular event and an approximately 2 to 4 times increased risk of later hypertension. Stroke risk may be increased.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The community-care plan specifies who provides follow-up, how often blood pressure is checked, thresholds for reducing or stopping treatment, and when to refer for a primary-care blood pressure review.

conditions.name: Pre-eclampsia
conditions.description: New hypertension, over 140 mmHg systolic or over 90 mmHg diastolic, after 20 weeks of pregnancy together with 1 or more newly occurring findings: proteinuria, maternal organ dysfunction or uteroplacental dysfunction.
conditions.epidemiology: The guideline states that less than 1 woman in every million who gives birth now dies from pre-eclampsia.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Possible symptoms include severe headache, blurred vision or flashing before the eyes, severe pain below the ribs, vomiting, and sudden swelling of the face, hands or feet. Maternal organ dysfunction may affect the kidneys, liver, nervous system or blood. Uteroplacental findings may include fetal growth restriction, abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform analysis or stillbirth.

subtypes.name: Severe pre-eclampsia
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Pre-eclampsia with severe hypertension unresponsive to treatment or accompanied by specified persistent symptoms, worsening blood results, impaired fetal growth or abnormal doppler findings.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate maternal and fetal wellbeing and determine whether hospital surveillance is needed.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At every antenatal appointment, by a healthcare professional trained in managing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Concerning findings include sustained systolic blood pressure of 160 mmHg or higher; a new, persistent rise in creatinine to 90 micromol/litre or more, 1 mg/100 ml or more; a rise in alanine transaminase to over 70 IU/litre, or twice upper limit of normal range; a fall in platelet count to under 150,000/microlitre; impending eclampsia or pulmonary oedema; other severe features; or suspected fetal compromise.

diagnostic_workup.test: Automated reagent-strip reading device for dipstick proteinuria screening
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Screen for urinary protein in secondary care.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of a pregnant woman for proteinuria.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A screening result of 1+ or more calls for quantification with albumin:creatinine ratio or protein:creatinine ratio. For the definition of pre-eclampsia, dipstick proteinuria is at least 1 g/litre [2+].

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Quantify proteinuria.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: After a positive dipstick result of 1+ or more; a first morning urine void should not be used for quantification.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: 30 mg/mmol or more indicates significant proteinuria. If the result is 30 mg/mmol or above and diagnosis remains uncertain, consider testing a new sample alongside clinical review.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide an alternative measure of proteinuria when diagnosing pre-eclampsia in a pregnant woman with hypertension.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: After a positive dipstick result of 1+ or more; a first morning urine void should not be used for quantification.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The diagnostic threshold is 8 mg/mmol. If the result is 8 mg/mmol or above and diagnosis remains uncertain, consider testing a new sample alongside clinical review.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Quantify proteinuria.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not for routine use; the guideline notes that it may be more appropriate on rare occasions, such as in women with renal complications.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help rule out pre-eclampsia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: For suspected pre-eclampsia between 20 weeks and 36 weeks and 6 days of pregnancy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess renal involvement and monitor maternal condition.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment and subsequent blood-test monitoring.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Creatinine of 90 micromol/litre or more, 1.02 mg/100 ml or more, is a renal-insufficiency criterion in the definition of pre-eclampsia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess liver involvement and monitor maternal condition.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment and subsequent blood-test monitoring.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase over 40 IU/litre is a liver-involvement criterion in the definition of pre-eclampsia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess haematological involvement and monitor maternal condition.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment and subsequent blood-test monitoring.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A count below 150,000/microlitre is a thrombocytopenia criterion in the definition of pre-eclampsia.

diagnostic_workup.test: Full blood count, liver function and renal function
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Monitor maternal haematological, liver and kidney status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Twice a week with hypertension or 3 times a week with severe hypertension.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal heart activity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At every antenatal appointment.

diagnostic_workup.test: Ultrasound for fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume assessment
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis and, if normal, every 2 weeks.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the fetal circulation and uteroplacental dysfunction.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis if conservative management is planned; repeat fetal growth, amniotic fluid or umbilical artery doppler assessment every 2 weeks according to findings.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform may indicate uteroplacental dysfunction.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis; subsequently if clinically indicated, including a change in fetal movement, vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain or deterioration in maternal condition.

prognostic_tools.name: fullPIERS
prognostic_tools.interpretation: May help guide place-of-care and intervention decisions at any time during pregnancy by predicting adverse maternal outcomes; it does not predict outcomes for babies.

prognostic_tools.name: PREP-S
prognostic_tools.interpretation: May help guide place-of-care and intervention decisions only up to 34 weeks of pregnancy by predicting adverse maternal outcomes; it does not predict outcomes for babies.

follow_up.schedule: After transfer to community care, offer a review at 2 weeks to women who remain on antihypertensive treatment. Offer all women a medical review 6 to 8 weeks after birth. Persistent proteinuria of 1+ or more at that review calls for a further kidney-function review at 3 months.
recommended_tests: For women who received no antihypertensive treatment, measure blood pressure at least 4 times a day while admitted, at least once between day 3 and day 5 after birth, and on alternate days until normal if it was abnormal on days 3 to 5.

For women who received antihypertensive treatment, measure blood pressure at least 4 times a day while admitted and every 1 to 2 days for up to 2 weeks after transfer to community care, until treatment has stopped and hypertension has resolved.
Ask about severe headache and epigastric pain whenever blood pressure is measured after birth.

For mild or moderate hypertension, or after step-down from critical care, measure platelet count, transaminases and serum creatinine 48 to 72 hours after birth or step-down; do not repeat normal measurements at that time. Repeat abnormal results as clinically indicated until normal.
Perform a urinary reagent-strip test 6 to 8 weeks after birth; assess kidney function at 3 months if proteinuria remains 1+ or more.
long_term_effects: After pre-eclampsia in a previous or current pregnancy, hypertension of any type in a future pregnancy occurs in approximately 20% (1 in 5 women), and pre-eclampsia in up to approximately 16% (1 in 6 women). If birth was at 28 to 34 weeks, the reported recurrence of pre-eclampsia is approximately 33% (1 in 3 women); if birth was at 34 to 37 weeks, it is approximately 23% (1 in 4 women).

No evidence was identified for recurrence after birth at less than 28 weeks; the committee considered the risk likely to be at least as high as, if not higher than, after birth between 28 and 34 weeks.

After pre-eclampsia in a previous or current pregnancy, the table reports future gestational hypertension in between approximately 6 and 12% (up to 1 in 8 women) and chronic hypertension in approximately 2% (up to 1 in 50 women).

For women with pre-eclampsia in a current or previous pregnancy, the table reports an approximately 1.5 to 3 times increased risk of a major adverse cardiovascular event, an approximately 2 times increased risk of cardiovascular mortality, an approximately 2 to 3 times increased risk of stroke, and an approximately 2 to 5 times increased risk of later hypertension.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: If neither proteinuria nor hypertension is present at the postnatal review at 6 to 8 weeks, the guideline states that the relative risk of end-stage kidney disease remains increased but its absolute risk is low, and no further follow-up is necessary. Consider specialist kidney assessment if kidney function is abnormal at 3 months. Women are advised to reach and maintain a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2 before a subsequent pregnancy; recurrence becomes more likely when the inter-pregnancy interval exceeds 10 years.

conditions.name: Severe pre-eclampsia
conditions.description: Pre-eclampsia with severe hypertension that does not respond to treatment, or with ongoing or recurrent severe symptoms, progressively worsening blood tests, impaired fetal growth or abnormal doppler findings.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Features may include persistent or recurrent severe headache, visual scotomata, nausea or vomiting, epigastric pain, oliguria with severe hypertension, rising creatinine or liver transaminases, falling platelet count, impaired fetal growth or abnormal doppler findings.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess severity and response to treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Every 15 to 30 minutes until blood pressure is less than 160/110 mmHg; thereafter at least 4 times daily while admitted, according to clinical circumstances.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Failure to control maternal blood pressure despite 3 or more classes of antihypertensives in appropriate doses is a possible threshold for considering planned early birth.

diagnostic_workup.test: Full blood count, liver function and renal function
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect and monitor worsening maternal haematological, liver or kidney status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: 3 times a week when pre-eclampsia is accompanied by severe hypertension.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Progressive deterioration in liver function, renal function, haemolysis or platelet count may support consideration of planned early birth.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess oxygenation when considering maternal indications for early birth.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During evaluation of severe features.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A reading less than 90% is a possible threshold for considering planned early birth. Some devices may underestimate or overestimate saturation, particularly near a borderline value; overestimation has been reported in people with dark skin.

diagnostic_workup.test: Ultrasound for fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume assessment
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal growth and condition.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis and, if normal, every 2 weeks.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Failure of fetal growth is among the features included in the definition of severe pre-eclampsia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal circulation and help identify fetal indications for birth.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis if conservative management is planned; repeat assessment every 2 weeks according to findings.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Abnormal doppler findings are among the features of severe pre-eclampsia; reversed end-diastolic flow may be considered when deciding on early birth.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fetal status.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis and again if clinically indicated, including a change in fetal movement, vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain or deterioration in maternal condition.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A nonreassuring cardiotocograph may be considered when deciding on early birth.

prognostic_tools.name: fullPIERS
prognostic_tools.interpretation: May help guide maternal place-of-care and intervention decisions at any time during pregnancy; it does not predict outcomes for babies.

prognostic_tools.name: PREP-S
prognostic_tools.interpretation: May help guide maternal place-of-care and intervention decisions only up to 34 weeks of pregnancy; it does not predict outcomes for babies.

follow_up.schedule: Postnatal follow-up follows the guidance for pre-eclampsia, including a medical review 6 to 8 weeks after birth.
recommended_tests: After step-down from critical care, measure platelet count, transaminases and serum creatinine at 48 to 72 hours; repeat abnormal results as clinically indicated until normal.

conditions.name: Eclampsia
conditions.description: A convulsive condition occurring in association with pre-eclampsia.
conditions.clinical_presentation: An eclamptic fit may occur alongside severe hypertension or severe pre-eclampsia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify an eclamptic fit and determine the need for critical care.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When a fit occurs or has occurred in a woman with severe hypertension or severe pre-eclampsia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Eclampsia is listed among complications meeting the guideline's criteria for Level 2 care in severe pre-eclampsia.

conditions.name: HELLP syndrome
conditions.description: A syndrome characterised by haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and a low platelet count.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of haemolysis, liver enzymes and platelet count
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify the components used to describe HELLP syndrome.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The named components are haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelet count; the guideline supplies no separate diagnostic thresholds for HELLP syndrome.

special_populations.population: Pregnant women at high risk of pre-eclampsia
special_populations.considerations: High-risk factors are hypertensive disease in a previous pregnancy, chronic kidney disease, autoimmune disease such as systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome, type 1 or type 2 diabetes, or chronic hypertension.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Advise aspirin 75 mg to 150 mg daily from 12 weeks until the birth of the baby.

special_populations.population: Pregnant women with more than 1 moderate risk factor for pre-eclampsia
special_populations.considerations: Moderate risk factors are nulliparity, age 40 years or older, a pregnancy interval of more than 10 years, BMI of 35 kg/m2 or more at the first visit, a family history of pre-eclampsia, and multi-fetal pregnancy.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Advise aspirin 75 mg to 150 mg daily from 12 weeks until the birth of the baby.

special_populations.population: Women with pre-existing diabetes or gestational diabetes
special_populations.considerations: The guideline directs care for these women to the NICE guideline on diabetes in pregnancy.

special_populations.population: Women with chronic hypertension planning pregnancy or becoming pregnant
special_populations.considerations: ACE inhibitors and ARBs carry an increased risk of congenital abnormalities when taken during pregnancy. Thiazide or thiazide-like diuretics may increase the risk of congenital abnormalities and neonatal complications. Women planning pregnancy should discuss alternative treatment with the professional managing their condition.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: If pregnancy occurs while taking ACE inhibitors or ARBs, stop that treatment, preferably within 2 working days of notification of pregnancy, and offer an alternative.

special_populations.population: Pregnant women with renal complications undergoing proteinuria assessment
special_populations.considerations: Although 24-hour urine collection should not routinely be used to quantify proteinuria, the guideline notes rare circumstances, such as renal complications, in which it may be more appropriate.

special_populations.population: Women with previous severe pre-eclampsia or other specified adverse pregnancy outcomes
special_populations.considerations: Additional fetal monitoring applies after severe pre-eclampsia, pre-eclampsia resulting in birth before 34 weeks, pre-eclampsia with a baby's birth weight below the 10th centile, intrauterine death, or placental abruption.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Start ultrasound assessment of fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume, with umbilical artery doppler velocimetry, between 28 and 30 weeks, or at least 2 weeks before the previous gestational age of onset if that was earlier than 28 weeks; repeat 4 weeks later. Carry out cardiotocography only if clinically indicated.

special_populations.population: Women with pre-eclampsia or hypertension associated with early birth before 34 weeks
special_populations.considerations: In a future pregnancy, recurrent hypertensive disorders are a concern.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Consider counselling before pregnancy about recurrence risk and ways to lower it.

special_populations.population: Women with a history of pre-eclampsia and an inter-pregnancy interval greater than 10 years
special_populations.considerations: The likelihood of recurrent pre-eclampsia increases when the interval between pregnancies exceeds 10 years.

special_populations.population: Women with a history of pre-eclampsia and no proteinuria or hypertension at postnatal review
special_populations.considerations: At the review 6 to 8 weeks after birth, the relative risk of end-stage kidney disease remains increased, but the absolute risk is low.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Advise that no further follow-up is necessary when neither proteinuria nor hypertension is present at that review.

special_populations.population: Women with persistent proteinuria or abnormal kidney function after pre-eclampsia
special_populations.considerations: Proteinuria of 1+ or more at 6 to 8 weeks after birth warrants further assessment of kidney function. An abnormal kidney assessment at 3 months may warrant specialist review.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Offer a further review with a GP or specialist at 3 months after birth if proteinuria persists; consider referral for specialist kidney assessment if kidney function is abnormal at 3 months.

special_populations.population: Women of black African or Caribbean family origin with postnatal hypertension
special_populations.considerations: The guideline identifies separate postnatal antihypertensive options for this population.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Consider nifedipine, or amlodipine if it previously controlled the woman's blood pressure successfully.

special_populations.population: Women with hypertension who wish to breastfeed or express milk
special_populations.considerations: Antihypertensive treatment can be adapted to allow breastfeeding; needing medication does not itself prevent breastfeeding. Most antihypertensive medicines taken while breastfeeding produce very low levels in breast milk, although the medicines can pass into it.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Make treatment decisions with the woman according to her preferences. Where possible, avoid diuretics or angiotensin receptor blockers during breastfeeding or milk expression.

special_populations.population: Babies of women taking antihypertensive medicines while breastfeeding
special_populations.considerations: Transfer of antihypertensive medicines into breast milk creates a potential need to watch for low blood pressure, particularly in babies born preterm.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Consider blood-pressure monitoring during the first few weeks for babies with symptoms of low blood pressure, especially those born preterm. After discharge, advise women to watch for drowsiness, lethargy, pallor, cold peripheries or poor feeding.

special_populations.population: Women with postnatal hypertension who are not breastfeeding and do not plan to breastfeed
special_populations.considerations: The guideline distinguishes their treatment from treatment during breastfeeding.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Manage hypertension in line with the NICE guideline on hypertension in adults.

special_populations.population: Neonates exposed to prolonged or repeated maternal magnesium sulfate during pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: Maternal magnesium sulfate use for longer than 5 to 7 days during pregnancy has been associated with neonatal skeletal adverse effects, hypocalcaemia and hypermagnesemia.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: If maternal use is prolonged or repeated, consider monitoring the neonate for abnormal calcium and magnesium levels and skeletal adverse effects.

special_populations.population: People with dark skin undergoing pulse oximetry
special_populations.considerations: Pulse oximeters may overestimate oxygen saturation in people with dark skin. Some devices may underestimate or overestimate saturation, particularly when the reading is borderline.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with gestational hypertension without severe hypertension.
decision_rules: Arrange a comprehensive assessment in secondary care by a professional trained in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

Account for nulliparity, age 40 years or older, pregnancy interval of more than 10 years, family history of pre-eclampsia, multi-fetal pregnancy, BMI of 35 kg/m2 or more, gestational age at presentation, previous pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension, and pre-existing vascular or kidney disease when deciding on additional assessment and follow-up.
Do not routinely admit to hospital; offer medicine if blood pressure remains above 140/90 mmHg and aim for 135/85 mmHg or less once treated.
Consider labetalol, then nifedipine if labetalol is unsuitable, then methyldopa if neither is suitable. Consider adverse effects, risks including fetal effects, and the woman's preferences.
If pre-eclampsia is suspected between 20 weeks and 36 weeks and 6 days, offer PLGF-based testing to help rule it out.

recommended_regimens.name: labetalol
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider to treat gestational hypertension when pharmacological treatment is needed.

alternative_regimens.name: methyldopa
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.

not_recommended.reason: Do not offer it as treatment for gestational hypertension.

response_assessment.method: Test urine protein with a dipstick.

response_assessment.method: Auscultate the fetal heart.

response_assessment.method: Perform PLGF-based testing.
response_assessment.interpretation: Use to help rule out pre-eclampsia.

supportive_care: Perform cardiotocography only if clinically indicated.
At diagnosis, assess fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume by ultrasound and perform umbilical artery doppler velocimetry; if findings are normal, repeat every 2 to 4 weeks if clinically indicated.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: At publication (June 2019), some nifedipine brands were specifically contraindicated by their manufacturers during pregnancy.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with severe gestational hypertension.
decision_rules: Admit to hospital and offer pharmacological antihypertensive treatment to all women.
If blood pressure falls below 160/110 mmHg, follow the management approach for gestational hypertension without severe hypertension.
Aim for blood pressure of 135/85 mmHg or less on treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: labetalol
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider as the preferred named treatment option for gestational hypertension.

alternative_regimens.name: nifedipine
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider as an alternative treatment for gestational hypertension.

alternative_regimens.name: methyldopa
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider as a further alternative treatment for gestational hypertension.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.

not_recommended.name: bed rest in hospital
not_recommended.reason: Do not offer it as treatment for gestational hypertension.

response_assessment.timepoint: Every 15 to 30 minutes until blood pressure is less than 160/110 mmHg
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure.
response_assessment.interpretation: Once treated, aim for 135/85 mmHg or less.

response_assessment.timepoint: Daily while admitted
response_assessment.method: Perform dipstick proteinuria testing.

response_assessment.timepoint: At presentation and then weekly
response_assessment.method: Measure full blood count, liver function and renal function.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis; every 2 weeks thereafter if the initial ultrasound is normal and severe hypertension persists
response_assessment.method: Assess the fetus by ultrasound.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis; repeat only if clinically indicated
response_assessment.method: Perform cardiotocography.

supportive_care: Auscultate the fetal heart at each antenatal appointment.
If pre-eclampsia is suspected, carry out PLGF-based testing on 1 occasion in accordance with the specified gestational-age window.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with gestational hypertension whose blood pressure is lower than 160/110 mmHg.
decision_rules: Do not offer planned early birth before 37 weeks unless another medical indication exists.
After 37 weeks, agree timing and maternal and fetal indications for birth between the woman and a senior obstetrician.
If planned early birth is needed, offer a course of antenatal corticosteroids and magnesium sulfate when indicated, in line with the NICE guideline on preterm labour and birth.

not_recommended.name: planned early birth before 37 weeks
not_recommended.reason: Do not offer when blood pressure is lower than 160/110 mmHg unless there are other medical indications.

supportive_care: Offer antenatal corticosteroids and magnesium sulfate if indicated when early birth is planned.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with gestational hypertension after birth.
decision_rules: Continue antihypertensive treatment if required, and reduce it if blood pressure falls below 130/ 80 mmHg.
For women who did not take antihypertensives, start treatment if blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg or higher.
If methyldopa was taken during pregnancy, stop it within 2 days after birth and change to another treatment if necessary.

recommended_regimens.name: antihypertensive treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Continue or initiate after birth according to blood pressure and prior treatment.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Postnatal treatment usually lasts a period similar to antenatal treatment, but may last longer.

response_assessment.timepoint: Daily for the first 2 days after birth; at least once between day 3 and day 5; as clinically indicated following treatment changes
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure.
response_assessment.interpretation: Reduce treatment if blood pressure falls below 130/ 80 mmHg.

response_assessment.timepoint: 2 weeks after transfer to community care
response_assessment.method: Offer a GP or specialist medical review if antihypertensive treatment continues.

response_assessment.timepoint: 6 to 8 weeks after birth
response_assessment.method: Offer all women a GP or specialist medical review.

supportive_care: At transfer to community care, document the follow-up provider, blood pressure monitoring frequency, thresholds for reducing or stopping treatment, and indications for primary care referral for blood pressure review.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with pre-eclampsia and hypertension that is not severe.
decision_rules: Have a professional trained in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy assess the woman and perform a full clinical assessment at every antenatal appointment.
Offer admission if maternal or fetal wellbeing causes concern or fullPIERS or PREP-S suggests a high risk of adverse events.
Offer pharmacological treatment if blood pressure remains above 140/90 mmHg; aim for 135/85 mmHg or less on treatment.

Offer labetalol; offer nifedipine if labetalol is unsuitable, or methyldopa if both are unsuitable. Consider previous treatment, adverse effects, risks including fetal effects, and patient preference.

recommended_regimens.name: labetalol
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer to treat hypertension associated with pre-eclampsia.

alternative_regimens.name: nifedipine
alternative_regimens.summary: Offer to treat hypertension associated with pre-eclampsia.

alternative_regimens.name: methyldopa
alternative_regimens.summary: Offer to treat hypertension associated with pre-eclampsia.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.

response_assessment.timepoint: At least every 48 hours; more often if admitted
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure.
response_assessment.interpretation: Aim for 135/85 mmHg or less during antihypertensive treatment.

response_assessment.timepoint: Twice a week
response_assessment.method: Measure full blood count, liver function and renal function.

response_assessment.timepoint: Only when clinically indicated
response_assessment.method: Repeat dipstick proteinuria testing.
response_assessment.interpretation: Examples include new symptoms or signs and diagnostic uncertainty.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis and, if normal, every 2 weeks
response_assessment.method: Perform fetal ultrasound assessment.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis; thereafter only if clinically indicated
response_assessment.method: Perform cardiotocography.

supportive_care: Auscultate the fetal heart at every antenatal appointment.

Consider fullPIERS or PREP-S alongside clinical assessment to inform place of care and intervention thresholds; fullPIERS can be used at any time in pregnancy, whereas PREP-S is intended only up to 34 weeks. Neither predicts infant outcomes.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Clinical concerns warranting admission may include sustained systolic blood pressure of 160 mmHg or higher, concerning maternal blood results, impending eclampsia or pulmonary oedema, other severe pre-eclampsia features, or suspected fetal compromise. At publication (June 2019), some nifedipine brands were specifically contraindicated during pregnancy by their manufacturers.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with pre-eclampsia and severe hypertension.
decision_rules: Admit and offer antihypertensive medicine to all women.
If blood pressure falls below 160/ 110 mmHg, manage according to the non-severe hypertension pathway.
Aim for blood pressure of 135/85 mmHg or less on treatment.
Use the pre-eclampsia antihypertensive sequence: offer labetalol, then nifedipine if unsuitable, then methyldopa if neither is suitable.

recommended_regimens.name: labetalol
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer for hypertension in pre-eclampsia.

alternative_regimens.name: methyldopa
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When labetalol and nifedipine are unsuitable.

response_assessment.timepoint: Every 15 to 30 minutes until blood pressure is less than 160/110 mmHg; then at least 4 times daily while an inpatient, according to clinical circumstances
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure.
response_assessment.interpretation: Aim for 135/85 mmHg or less once treated.

response_assessment.timepoint: 3 times a week
response_assessment.method: Measure full blood count, liver function and renal function.

response_assessment.timepoint: Only when clinically indicated
response_assessment.method: Repeat dipstick proteinuria testing.
response_assessment.interpretation: Examples include new symptoms or signs and diagnostic uncertainty.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis and, if normal, every 2 weeks
response_assessment.method: Assess the fetus by ultrasound.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis; subsequently only if clinically indicated
response_assessment.method: Perform cardiotocography.

supportive_care: Auscultate the fetal heart at every antenatal appointment.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Escalate care according to maternal complications and the critical care criteria.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with pre-eclampsia before 34 weeks for whom continued pregnancy is being considered.
decision_rules: Continue surveillance unless maternal or fetal indications justify planned early birth.

Document maternal and fetal thresholds for birth before 37 weeks. Possible thresholds include failure to control blood pressure despite 3 or more antihypertensive classes at appropriate doses, maternal pulse oximetry less than 90%, worsening liver or kidney function, haemolysis or platelet count, persistent neurological features, placental abruption, reversed end-diastolic umbilical artery flow, a nonreassuring cardiotocograph, or stillbirth.
Involve a senior obstetrician in birth-timing decisions; discuss planned birth with the anaesthetic team and, if neonatal complications are anticipated, the neonatal team.

recommended_regimens.name: intravenous magnesium sulfate
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer in line with the NICE guideline on preterm labour and birth.

recommended_regimens.name: antenatal corticosteroids
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer a course in line with the NICE guideline on preterm labour and birth.

response_assessment.timepoint: During continued surveillance before 34 weeks
response_assessment.method: Assess maternal and fetal condition against the recorded thresholds for early birth.
response_assessment.interpretation: Consider planned early birth when an indication arises; the specified features are not an exhaustive list.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Some pulse oximeters can under- or overestimate oxygen saturation, particularly near a threshold; overestimation has been reported in people with dark skin.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with pre-eclampsia from 34 weeks to 36 weeks plus 6 days.
decision_rules: Continue surveillance unless maternal or fetal indications warrant planned early birth.
When considering early birth, account for the woman's and baby's condition, maternal comorbidities, multi-fetal pregnancy and neonatal unit bed availability.
Involve a senior obstetrician in timing decisions and discuss planned birth with the anaesthetic team and, when neonatal complications are anticipated, the neonatal team.

alternative_regimens.name: antenatal corticosteroids
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider a course in line with the NICE guideline on preterm labour and birth.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When planned early birth is being considered.

response_assessment.timepoint: From 34 weeks to 36 weeks plus 6 days
response_assessment.method: Continue maternal and fetal surveillance and evaluate indications for early birth.
response_assessment.interpretation: An indication for early birth changes the surveillance-first approach.

supportive_care: If early birth is planned for preterm pre-eclampsia, offer intravenous magnesium sulfate and antenatal corticosteroids when indicated, in line with the NICE guideline on preterm labour and birth.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with pre-eclampsia from 37 weeks onwards.
decision_rules: Initiate birth within 24 to 48 hours.
Involve a senior obstetrician in the timing decision, discuss planned birth with the anaesthetic team, and involve the neonatal team if neonatal complications are anticipated.

recommended_regimens.name: birth
recommended_regimens.summary: Initiate birth for pre-eclampsia from 37 weeks onwards.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with pre-eclampsia after birth who did not take antihypertensive treatment.
decision_rules: Start antihypertensive treatment if blood pressure is 150/ 100 mmHg or higher.
At every blood pressure measurement, ask about severe headache and epigastric pain.
Offer transfer to community care only when pre-eclampsia symptoms are absent, blood pressure with or without treatment is 150/100 mmHg or less, and blood results are stable or improving.

recommended_regimens.name: antihypertensive treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Start after birth when the specified blood pressure threshold is reached.

response_assessment.timepoint: At least 4 times a day while an inpatient; at least once between day 3 and day 5 after birth; on alternate days until normal if blood pressure was abnormal on days 3 to 5
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure and ask about severe headache and epigastric pain.
response_assessment.interpretation: Start treatment at 150/ 100 mmHg or higher.

response_assessment.timepoint: 6 to 8 weeks after birth
response_assessment.method: Offer a GP or specialist medical review and perform a urinary reagent-strip test.
response_assessment.interpretation: Proteinuria of 1+ or more requires a further review at 3 months to assess kidney function.

response_assessment.timepoint: 3 months after birth if proteinuria persists at 6 to 8 weeks
response_assessment.method: Assess kidney function with a GP or specialist.
response_assessment.interpretation: Consider specialist kidney assessment if kidney function is abnormal.

supportive_care: At community transfer, document the follow-up provider, blood pressure monitoring frequency, treatment reduction or cessation thresholds, primary care referral indications and symptom self-monitoring.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with pre-eclampsia after birth who took antihypertensive treatment.
decision_rules: Continue antihypertensive treatment; consider reducing it if blood pressure falls below 140/90 mmHg and reduce it if blood pressure falls below 130/ 80 mmHg.
Stop methyldopa within 2 days after birth and change treatment if needed.
Transfer to community care only if symptoms have resolved, blood pressure with or without treatment is 150/100 mmHg or less, and blood results are stable or improving.

recommended_regimens.name: antihypertensive treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Continue after birth, adjusting treatment to blood pressure.

response_assessment.timepoint: At least 4 times a day while an inpatient; every 1 to 2 days for up to 2 weeks after transfer to community care until off treatment and without hypertension
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure and ask about severe headache and epigastric pain.
response_assessment.interpretation: Consider dose reduction below 140/90 mmHg and reduce treatment below 130/ 80 mmHg.

response_assessment.timepoint: 2 weeks after transfer to community care, if treatment continues
response_assessment.method: Offer a GP or specialist medical review.

response_assessment.timepoint: 6 to 8 weeks after birth
response_assessment.method: Offer a GP or specialist medical review and perform a urinary reagent-strip test.
response_assessment.interpretation: If proteinuria is still 1+ or more, arrange kidney function review at 3 months.

supportive_care: Provide a community care plan specifying follow-up, blood pressure checks, treatment adjustment thresholds, primary care referral indications and symptom self-monitoring.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women after birth with pre-eclampsia and mild or moderate hypertension, or stepping down from critical care.
decision_rules: Do not repeat platelet count, transaminases or serum creatinine if results are normal at 48 to 72 hours.
If haematological or biochemical results are outside the reference range, repeat tests as clinically indicated until they return to normal.

response_assessment.timepoint: 48 to 72 hours after birth or step-down from critical care
response_assessment.method: Measure platelet count, transaminases and serum creatinine.
response_assessment.interpretation: Normal results do not require repeat measurement; abnormal results require clinically indicated repeat testing until normal.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant women with pre-eclampsia or severe gestational hypertension undergoing fetal surveillance.
decision_rules: Perform cardiotocography at diagnosis.
If conservative management is planned, assess fetal growth and amniotic fluid by ultrasound and perform umbilical artery doppler velocimetry at diagnosis.
If all fetal monitoring results are normal, do not routinely repeat cardiotocography unless clinically indicated.
Repeat cardiotocography if fetal movements change, vaginal bleeding or abdominal pain occurs, or the maternal condition deteriorates.

response_assessment.timepoint: At diagnosis
response_assessment.method: Perform cardiotocography; if conservative management is planned, also perform fetal growth and amniotic fluid ultrasound and umbilical artery doppler velocimetry.

response_assessment.timepoint: Every 2 weeks
response_assessment.method: Repeat fetal growth and amniotic fluid ultrasound or umbilical artery doppler velocimetry.
response_assessment.interpretation: Determine subsequent surveillance from scan findings.

response_assessment.timepoint: If fetal movement changes, vaginal bleeding or abdominal pain occurs, or maternal condition deteriorates
response_assessment.method: Repeat cardiotocography.

supportive_care: Document the timing and type of future fetal monitoring, fetal indications for birth, whether and when antenatal corticosteroids should be given, and plans to consult neonatal paediatricians and obstetric anaesthetists.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women in labour with a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy.
decision_rules: Continue antenatal antihypertensive treatment during labour.
Follow the NICE guideline on intrapartum care unless this guideline addresses the same subject; care for hypertension should not be based solely on blood pressure during labour.
Use the antenatal criteria to decide whether haematological and biochemical testing is needed, even when regional analgesia is considered.

recommended_regimens.name: antenatal antihypertensive treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Continue the existing antenatal treatment during labour.

response_assessment.timepoint: Hourly during labour
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure in women with hypertension.

response_assessment.timepoint: Every 15 to 30 minutes until blood pressure is less than 160/110 mmHg
response_assessment.method: Measure blood pressure in women with severe hypertension.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: For women with chronic hypertension, also follow the NICE guideline on intrapartum care for women with existing medical conditions or obstetric complications and their babies.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with severe pre-eclampsia receiving epidural analgesia or requiring a decision about mode of birth.
decision_rules: Do not preload with intravenous fluids before low-dose epidural or combined spinal epidural analgesia.
Choose mode of birth according to clinical circumstances and the woman's preference.

not_recommended.name: intravenous fluid preload
not_recommended.reason: Do not give before establishing low-dose epidural or combined spinal epidural analgesia in severe pre-eclampsia.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women in the second stage of labour whose severe hypertension has not responded to initial treatment.
decision_rules: Consider operative or assisted birth during the second stage when severe hypertension does not respond to initial treatment.
Do not routinely limit the second stage solely because a woman has controlled hypertension.

alternative_regimens.name: operative or assisted birth
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider in the second stage of labour.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Severe hypertension has not responded to initial treatment.

not_recommended.name: routine limitation of the second stage of labour
not_recommended.reason: Do not routinely limit its duration in women with controlled hypertension.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women in critical care with severe hypertension or severe pre-eclampsia who have had an eclamptic fit, including a previous fit.
decision_rules: Give intravenous magnesium sulfate using the Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen.
Treat recurrent fits with a further intravenous magnesium sulfate dose.
Do not substitute diazepam, phenytoin or other anticonvulsants for magnesium sulfate.

recommended_regimens.name: Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen
recommended_regimens.summary: Administer intravenous magnesium sulfate for eclamptic fits.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Loading dose of 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes, followed by 1 g/hour for 24 hours; after an eclamptic fit, continue the infusion for 24 hours after the last fit. For recurrent fits, give a further 2 g to 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes.

not_recommended.name: diazepam
not_recommended.reason: Do not use as an alternative to magnesium sulfate in eclampsia.

not_recommended.name: phenytoin
not_recommended.reason: Do not use as an alternative to magnesium sulfate in eclampsia.

not_recommended.name: other anticonvulsants
not_recommended.reason: Do not use as alternatives to magnesium sulfate in eclampsia.

supportive_care: If magnesium sulfate use during pregnancy is prolonged or repeated, consider neonatal monitoring for abnormal calcium and magnesium levels and skeletal adverse effects.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Maternal magnesium sulfate administration for longer than 5 to 7 days in pregnancy has been associated with neonatal skeletal adverse effects, hypocalcaemia and hypermagnesemia.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with severe pre-eclampsia in critical care for whom birth is planned within 24 hours or who have features indicating a need to consider anticonvulsant treatment.
decision_rules: Consider intravenous magnesium sulfate if birth is planned within 24 hours.

Consider the need for magnesium sulfate when 1 or more of the following is present: persistent or recurrent severe headache, visual scotomata, nausea or vomiting, epigastric pain, oliguria with severe hypertension, or progressive worsening of blood tests.

alternative_regimens.name: Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider intravenous magnesium sulfate; if given, use the specified regimen.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Birth is planned within 24 hours in critical care, or features of severe pre-eclampsia warrant consideration of treatment.

response_assessment.timepoint: During critical care
response_assessment.method: Assess severe headache, visual scotomata, nausea or vomiting, epigastric pain, oliguria, blood pressure, creatinine, liver transaminases and platelet count.
response_assessment.interpretation: The listed findings inform consideration of magnesium sulfate.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen uses 4 g intravenously over 5 to 15 minutes, followed by 1 g/hour for 24 hours.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with severe hypertension in critical care during pregnancy or after birth.
decision_rules: Treat immediately with 1 of the named antihypertensive options.
Monitor blood pressure reduction, adverse effects in the woman and baby, and the need to change treatment according to response.

recommended_regimens.name: labetalol
recommended_regimens.summary: Give orally or intravenously as an immediate treatment option.

recommended_regimens.name: nifedipine
recommended_regimens.summary: Give orally as an immediate treatment option.

recommended_regimens.name: hydralazine
recommended_regimens.summary: Give intravenously as an immediate treatment option.

response_assessment.timepoint: During immediate treatment
response_assessment.method: Monitor blood pressure and adverse effects in the woman and baby.
response_assessment.interpretation: Confirm that blood pressure falls and modify treatment according to response.

supportive_care: During the antenatal period, consider up to 500 ml crystalloid fluid before or alongside the first intravenous hydralazine dose.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Some nifedipine brands were specifically contraindicated by their manufacturers during pregnancy at publication (June 2019).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with severe pre-eclampsia in critical care.
decision_rules: Do not use volume expansion unless hydralazine is the antenatal antihypertensive.
Limit maintenance fluids to 80 ml/hour unless there are additional ongoing fluid losses, such as haemorrhage.

Select the critical care level according to clinical need: level 3 for severe pre-eclampsia requiring ventilation; level 2 for step-down from level 3 or severe pre-eclampsia with specified complications; level 1 for pre-eclampsia with hypertension, ongoing conservative antenatal management of severe preterm hypertension, or step-down treatment after birth.

not_recommended.name: volume expansion
not_recommended.reason: Do not use in severe pre-eclampsia unless hydralazine is the antenatal antihypertensive.

supportive_care: Limit maintenance fluids to 80 ml/hour unless other ongoing fluid losses occur.
Consider up to 500 ml crystalloid before or at the first intravenous hydralazine dose during the antenatal period.
